verdict_text:
YES

The script casts exactly the 112 named projection matrices with `.to(torch.bfloat16)`, leaves every other tensor as float32 with unchanged values, deletes nothing (the `buffer_re` with the always-failing `(?!)` lookahead never matches, which is harmless here since there are no buffers), preserves names, and asserts all four required checks before writing. The only part I cannot verify from reading is the shard-size and index behaviour, which lives in the unshown `_ckpt.save_sharded_safetensors` helper; the caller passes the correct 268,435,456-byte limit.
note: experimenter: set `detected` (true if the stated problem matches expected_defect; for a correct artifact, true means a false alarm).
